auto-loan.guideTitle: How Auto Loan Financing & Monthly Payments Work
auto-loan.guideDesc: Auto loans use amortization calculations where every monthly payment is divided between principal reduction and interest charges.
formulaLines: Monthly Payment (M) = P × [ r(1+r)^n ÷ ((1+r)^n - 1) ]
P = Loan Principal (Vehicle Price minus Down Payment)
r = Monthly Interest Rate (Annual Rate ÷ 12)
n = Total Number of Monthly Payments (Loan Term in Years × 12)

faq.question: How does a down payment affect an auto loan?
faq.answer: A larger down payment directly reduces the financed principal amount, lowering both your monthly payment and the total interest accrued over the life of the loan.

faq.question: Should I choose a 48-month or 72-month loan term?
faq.answer: Shorter terms (e.g. 48 months) have higher monthly payments but save significant money on overall interest. Longer terms lower monthly costs but increase total borrowing costs.

roi.guideTitle: How to Calculate Return on Investment (ROI) & Profitability
roi.guideDesc: Return on Investment evaluates the efficiency and profitability of an investment relative to its initial cost.
formulaLines: Basic ROI (%) = [(Net Profit) ÷ (Cost of Investment)] × 100
Net Profit = Final Investment Value - Initial Investment Cost
Annualized ROI (%) = [(1 + Basic ROI)^(1 ÷ Years) - 1] × 100

faq.question: What is Annualized ROI?
faq.answer: Annualized ROI measures the average geometric annual growth rate of an investment, allowing fair comparison across different time periods.

faq.question: Can ROI be negative?
faq.answer: Yes, a negative ROI indicates that the investment incurred a net financial loss relative to its initial outlay.

margin.guideTitle: How Profit Margin & Markup Pricing Are Calculated
margin.guideDesc: Profit Margin calculates profit relative to revenue, while Markup calculates profit relative to product cost.
formulaLines: Gross Profit = Revenue - Cost
Profit Margin (%) = (Gross Profit ÷ Revenue) × 100
Markup (%) = (Gross Profit ÷ Cost) × 100

faq.question: What is the main difference between Margin and Markup?
faq.answer: Margin uses total sales revenue as the denominator, whereas Markup uses initial cost as the denominator.

cap-rate.guideTitle: How Capitalization Rate (Cap Rate) Is Calculated in Real Estate
cap-rate.guideDesc: Cap Rate reflects the expected net rate of return produced by a commercial or residential real estate property.
formulaLines: Cap Rate (%) = (Net Operating Income ÷ Current Market Property Value) × 100
Net Operating Income (NOI) = Gross Rental Income - Operating Expenses

faq.question: What is considered a good Cap Rate?
faq.answer: Typically, a Cap Rate between 4% and 10% is common depending on market location, property risk, and asset condition.

freelance-net-income.guideTitle: How Freelance Net Income & Tax Deductions Are Calculated
freelance-net-income.guideDesc: Calculating net take-home earnings for independent contractors requires deducting business expenses from gross revenues, followed by self-employment and income taxes.
formulaLines: Taxable Profit = Gross Revenue - Eligible Business Expenses
Total Tax Liability = Income Tax + Self-Employment Tax
Net Take-Home Pay = Taxable Profit - Total Tax Liability

faq.question: What are eligible deductible business expenses?
faq.answer: Ordinary and necessary operating expenses incurred directly to run your business, such as software subscriptions, accounting fees, and office supplies.

debt-snowball.guideTitle: How the Debt Snowball Strategy Eliminates Debt
debt-snowball.guideDesc: The Debt Snowball method prioritizes paying off debts from smallest balance to largest balance to build momentum through quick psychological wins.
formulaLines: 1. List all debts ordered by remaining balance (smallest first)
2. Pay minimum required payments on all debts except the smallest
3. Roll all remaining extra budget into paying off the smallest debt
4. Once cleared, roll that entire monthly payment into the next debt

faq.question: How does Debt Snowball compare to Debt Avalanche?
faq.answer: Debt Snowball targets the smallest balance for psychological motivation, while Debt Avalanche targets the highest interest rate debt first to minimize total interest paid.

fuel-split.guideTitle: How Road Trip Fuel Costs & Passenger Bill Splits Are Calculated
fuel-split.guideDesc: Trip fuel calculations combine distance, vehicle fuel efficiency, fuel price per unit, and optional toll fees.
formulaLines: Fuel Needed (L) = Distance (km) ÷ Fuel Efficiency (km/L)
Total Trip Cost = (Fuel Needed × Fuel Price) + Tolls
Cost Per Person = Total Trip Cost ÷ Number of Passengers

faq.question: How should toll fees be split among passengers?
faq.answer: Tolls are added into the aggregate trip expenditure pool and divided equally among all carpool participants.

goal-savings.guideTitle: How to Calculate Required Monthly Savings for Financial Goals
goal-savings.guideDesc: Reaching a future financial target requires calculating monthly deposits accounting for initial capital and compound interest.
formulaLines: Future Value of Initial Capital = Initial Balance × (1 + r)^n
Remaining Target Gap = Goal Target Amount - Future Value of Initial
Monthly Contribution = Target Gap × [ r ÷ ((1 + r)^n - 1) ]

faq.question: What if interest rates fluctuate over time?
faq.answer: The calculator assumes a fixed return rate. Recalibrate your monthly target annually based on actual portfolio performance.

household-budget.guideTitle: How to Structure a Monthly Household Budget & Calculate Remaining Cash
household-budget.guideDesc: A healthy monthly household budget subtracts fixed housing, groceries, utilities, transportation, and planned savings from your net monthly income to keep cash flow positive.
formulaLines: Total Living Expenses = Housing + Groceries + Utilities + Transportation
Total Outflows = Total Living Expenses + Savings
Remaining Balance = Monthly Net Income - Total Outflows

faq.question: How is the remaining amount after expenses calculated?
faq.answer: Remaining cash equals Monthly Net Income minus housing, groceries, utilities, transportation, and monthly savings. Positive values are surplus; negative values indicate a deficit.

faq.question: What is the 50/30/20 household budget rule?
faq.answer: The 50/30/20 rule suggests spending up to 50% of net income on essentials, keeping 30% for flexible spending or discretionary cash, and saving at least 20%.

download-time.guideTitle: How File Download Times Are Calculated Based on Network Speed
download-time.guideDesc: Download duration depends on total file size, internet transfer speed, and network overhead losses.
formulaLines: 1 Byte = 8 Bits (Conversion factor)
Speed in Bytes/sec = Speed in Mbps × 1,000,000 ÷ 8
Download Time (seconds) = File Size (Bytes) ÷ Speed (Bytes/sec)

faq.question: What is the difference between Mbps and MB/s?
faq.answer: Mbps (Megabits per second) measures bandwidth speed provided by ISPs, whereas MB/s (Megabytes per second) measures saved file size. Divide Mbps by 8 to convert to MB/s.

peltier-cooling.guideDesc: Thermoelectric coolers transfer heat via the Peltier effect. Cooling capacity (Qc) and Coefficient of Performance (COP) depend on current, voltage, and delta temperature.
formulaLines: Power Consumption (Pin) = Voltage (V) × Current (I)
Coefficient of Performance (COP) = Cooling Capacity (Qc) ÷ Power Input (Pin)

faq.question: What is a typical Peltier COP?
faq.answer: Peltier COP usually ranges between 0.3 and 0.8 depending on delta-T. While less efficient than vapor compression, TECs provide silent solid-state cooling.

rent-vs-buy.guideTitle: Renting vs. Buying Real Estate Financial Analysis Guide
rent-vs-buy.guideDesc: Comparing renting versus buying a home evaluates equity accumulation and property appreciation against unrecoverable rent, interest, and maintenance costs.
formulaLines: Total Ownership Expense = Mortgage Interest + Property Taxes + Maintenance + HOA + Closing Costs
Home Equity Wealth = Property Market Value Growth - Remaining Mortgage Principal Balance
Total Renting Expense = Monthly Rent Paid + Rent Inflation + Renter Insurance - Investment Yields on Down Payment

faq.question: Is buying always better than renting long-term?
faq.answer: Not always. Renting can be financially superior if the unallocated down payment capital is invested in high-yielding index funds and property appreciation is modest.

mortgage.guideTitle: Mortgage Payment & Home Financing Amortization Guide
mortgage.guideDesc: A mortgage divides monthly payments into principal reduction, interest, property taxes, and homeowners insurance.
formulaLines: P = Loan Principal Amount
r = Monthly Interest Rate (Annual Rate ÷ 12)
n = Total Amortization Payments (Years × 12)

faq.question: How do extra principal payments affect a mortgage?
faq.answer: Making additional payments toward your loan principal shortens your overall payoff timeline and drastically reduces total interest expense.

compound.guideTitle: How Compound Interest Exponentially Grows Investment Wealth
compound.guideDesc: Compound interest earns interest on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest from prior periods.
compound.formulaHeading: Compound Interest Formula with Monthly Deposits
formulaLines: Total Future Value A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) + PMT × [ ((1 + r/n)^(nt) - 1) ÷ (r/n) ]
P = Initial Principal
PMT = Regular Monthly Contribution
r = Annual Interest Rate
n = Compounding Frequency per year
t = Time Horizon in Years

faq.question: Why is compounding frequency important?
faq.answer: More frequent compounding periods (e.g. daily vs annual) allow interest to generate additional yields faster over time.

unit.guideDesc: Unit conversion standardizes physical measurements across international system units (SI) and imperial systems.
formulaLines: Length: 1 Inch = 2.54 cm | 1 Meter = 3.28084 Feet
Mass: 1 Kilogram = 2.20462 Pounds
Temperature: °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32

faq.question: How accurate are these unit conversions?
faq.answer: All conversions utilize high-precision floating-point factors verified by international standards organizations (NIST / ISO).

bmi.guideTitle: Body Mass Index (BMI) & Weight Status Categories Guide
bmi.guideDesc: BMI measures body mass relative to height, serving as a general health screening metric defined by WHO.
formulaLines: Metric: BMI = Weight (kg) ÷ [Height (m)]²
Underweight: < 18.5 | Normal Weight: 18.5 - 24.9
Overweight: 25.0 - 29.9 | Obese: ≥ 30.0

faq.question: Is BMI accurate for athletes and bodybuilders?
faq.answer: BMI does not differentiate muscle mass from fat mass, so athletic individuals with high muscle density may score in the overweight category despite low body fat.

tip.guideDesc: Tip calculation applies a gratuity percentage to the pre-tax bill total and splits expenses evenly across group members.
formulaLines: Tip Amount = Bill Amount × (Tip Percentage ÷ 100)
Total Bill = Bill Amount + Tip Amount
Per Person Share = Total Bill ÷ Number of People

faq.question: Should tips be calculated before or after tax?
faq.answer: Standard etiquette recommends calculating gratuity on the pre-tax subtotal amount.

salary.guideTitle: Hourly, Monthly, & Annual Salary Conversion Guide
salary.guideDesc: Converting pay frequency translates hourly rates into weekly, bi-weekly, monthly, and annual gross compensation.
formulaLines: Annual Pay = Hourly Rate × Hours per Week × 52 Weeks
Monthly Pay = Annual Pay ÷ 12 Months
Weekly Pay = Annual Pay ÷ 52 Weeks

faq.question: How are paid vacation days accounted for?
faq.answer: The standard calculation assumes 52 paid weeks per year, including accrued paid time off (PTO).

age.guideTitle: Exact Calendar Age & Time Difference Guide
age.guideDesc: Calculating exact age computes elapsed calendar years, months, days, hours, and seconds accounting for leap years.
formulaLines: Total Years = Target Year - Birth Year (adjusted for month/day)
Total Days = Calendar Days difference including Leap Days
Leap Year Rule: Extra day added for years divisible by 4 (except century years not ÷ 400)

faq.question: How are leap years handled in age calculations?
faq.answer: Leap years add a 29th day to February, ensuring day counts between two calendar dates remain astronomically precise.

percentage.guideTitle: Percent Finder & How to Calculate Percentages Guide
percentage.guideDesc: Percentages express proportions as fractions of 100. Learn how to find a percentage of any number, calculate percentage changes, and how to use the percent key on any calculator.
formulaLines: Finding X% of Y = Total (Y) × [ Percentage (X) ÷ 100 ]
X is what % of Y = (Part ÷ Total) × 100
Percentage Change (%) = [(New Value - Original Value) ÷ Original Value] × 100
Discount Sale Price = Original Price × [ 1 - (Discount % ÷ 100) ]
Reverse Percentage (Original Total) = Partial Amount ÷ (Percentage ÷ 100)

faq.question: How can I find the percentage of a number?
faq.answer: To find a percentage of a number, divide the percentage by 100 to convert it into a decimal rate, then multiply it by the total number. For example, to find 20% of 150: 20 ÷ 100 = 0.20, then 0.20 × 150 = 30.

faq.question: How do you use the percent (%) key on a calculator?
faq.answer: On standard handheld or mobile calculators: 1) To find X% of Y, type Y × X % (e.g. 150 × 20 % outputs 30). 2) To add a percentage (like tax or tip), type Price + Rate % = (e.g. 100 + 15 % = 115). 3) To apply a discount, type Price - Discount % = (e.g. 80 - 25 % = 60).

faq.question: What is a Percent Finder tool?
faq.answer: A Percent Finder is an all-in-one calculator that solves multiple percentage calculations: finding a percentage of a total, calculating what percentage one number is of another, calculating percentage increase/decrease, finding discount prices, and solving reverse percentage problems.

faq.question: How do we find the percentage increase or decrease between two numbers?
faq.answer: Subtract the original value from the new value, divide the difference by the original value, and multiply by 100. A positive result indicates a percentage increase, while a negative result indicates a percentage decrease.

faq.question: How do I find what percentage one number is of another?
faq.answer: Divide the specific part by the total whole, then multiply by 100. For example, if you got 45 questions right out of 60 on a test: (45 ÷ 60) × 100 = 0.75 × 100 = 75%.

mortgage-affordability.guideTitle: How Lenders Calculate Mortgage Affordability & DTI Limits
mortgage-affordability.guideDesc: Mortgage affordability combines your gross monthly income, down payment cash, interest rate, and existing monthly debts using the banking 28%/36% Debt-to-Income (DTI) framework.
formulaLines: Front-End Housing Cap = Gross Monthly Income × 0.28
Back-End Total Debt Cap = (Gross Monthly Income × 0.36) - Existing Monthly Debts
Max Monthly Principal & Interest (M) = min(Front-End Cap, Back-End Cap)
Max Loan (P) = M × [ (1 - (1 + r)^(-n)) ÷ r ], Max Home Price = P + Down Payment

faq.question: What is the 28/36 rule in mortgage affordability?
faq.answer: Lenders typically cap housing costs (principal, interest, taxes, insurance) at 28% of gross monthly income and total debt payments (housing plus car loans, student loans, and credit cards) at 36%.

faq.question: How much does paying off a $400/month car loan increase home budget?
faq.answer: Under the 36% back-end DTI rule, eliminating $400 in monthly debt frees $400 of mortgage capacity—roughly $60,000 to $67,000 in additional buying power at 6%–7% over 30 years.

faq.question: Should I put 20% down or buy sooner with less down?
faq.answer: A 20% down payment eliminates Private Mortgage Insurance (PMI) and lowers monthly payments, while a smaller down payment preserves emergency cash reserves.

refinance.guideTitle: When Mortgage Refinancing Pays Off: Break-Even & Net Savings
refinance.guideDesc: Refinancing replaces your existing mortgage balance with a new interest rate and term. Calculating the closing-cost break-even month prevents overpaying if you plan to move soon.
formulaLines: Monthly Savings = Current Monthly Payment - New Monthly Payment
Break-Even Point (Months) = Closing Costs & Prepayment Fees ÷ Monthly Savings
Net Lifetime Savings = Remaining Current Interest - (New Total Interest + Closing Costs)

faq.question: What is the refinance break-even point?
faq.answer: It is the number of months required for your monthly payment reduction to repay upfront closing costs and prepayment penalties. For example, $3,000 in fees divided by $150/month savings equals a 20-month break-even.

faq.question: How much lower should the new interest rate be to refinance?
faq.answer: Traditionally a 0.75% to 1.0% drop made sense, though on large loan balances even a 0.50% reduction can pay off quickly if fees are low.

faq.question: Does resetting to a new 30-year term always save money?
faq.answer: Extending back to 30 years lowers monthly cash outflow, but can increase total interest paid unless you keep the remaining term equal or make extra principal payments.

vat.guideTitle: How to Add or Extract VAT & Sales Tax Without Rounding Errors
vat.guideDesc: Adding VAT multiplies the net price by (1 + rate), while extracting VAT from a tax-inclusive gross total requires dividing by (1 + rate)—not multiplying by the rate directly.
formulaLines: Add VAT: Gross Price = Net Price × (1 + VAT Rate)
Add VAT: Tax Amount = Net Price × VAT Rate
Remove VAT: Net Price = Gross Price ÷ (1 + VAT Rate)
Remove VAT: Tax Included = Gross Price - Net Price

faq.question: Why can't I subtract 18% from a VAT-inclusive price to get the net amount?
faq.answer: Because 18% VAT was added on top of 100%, making the gross price 118%. To reverse it accurately, divide the gross amount by 1.18—for example, 118 ÷ 1.18 = 100 net (18 VAT), whereas subtracting 18% of 118 would wrongly give 96.76.

faq.question: What is the standard VAT rate in Israel, EU, and the UK?
faq.answer: Israel's VAT is 18% (increased from 17% in 2025), the UK standard rate is 20%, and most EU countries range between 19% and 25%.

faq.question: How do businesses reclaim input VAT?
faq.answer: VAT-registered businesses subtract input VAT paid on supplier invoices from output VAT collected on customer sales when filing periodic returns.

break-even.guideTitle: How Break-Even Analysis & Contribution Margin Work
break-even.guideDesc: The break-even point tells you exactly how many units or dollars of revenue are required to cover fixed overhead and variable unit costs so profit reaches zero.
formulaLines: Contribution Margin per Unit = Selling Price - Variable Cost per Unit
Break-Even Units = Fixed Costs ÷ Contribution Margin per Unit
Contribution Margin Ratio = Contribution Margin per Unit ÷ Selling Price
Break-Even Revenue = Fixed Costs ÷ Contribution Margin Ratio

faq.question: What is Contribution Margin and why does it drive break-even?
faq.answer: Contribution margin is the money left over from each unit sold after paying variable costs (materials, shipping, fees). Every unit contributes that amount toward paying off fixed rent, payroll, and software costs.

faq.question: What happens if Variable Cost exceeds Selling Price?
faq.answer: Contribution margin becomes negative, meaning every additional sale loses money and the business can never break even without raising price or cutting per-unit cost.

faq.question: How do I calculate break-even for a target profit?
faq.answer: Add your desired monthly profit directly to Fixed Costs in the numerator: (Fixed Costs + Target Profit) ÷ Contribution Margin per Unit.

inflation.guideTitle: How Inflation Erodes Purchasing Power Over Time
inflation.guideDesc: Even modest annual inflation compounds relentlessly: at 3% inflation per year, prices double roughly every 24 years and idle cash loses almost half its real buying power.
inflation.formulaHeading: Future Cost & Real Purchasing Power Formulas
formulaLines: Future Equivalent Cost = Today's Cost × (1 + r)^t
Real Purchasing Power = Nominal Amount ÷ (1 + r)^t
Cumulative Inflation (%) = [ (1 + r)^t - 1 ] × 100
Real Investment Return ≈ [ (1 + Nominal Return) ÷ (1 + r) ] - 1

faq.question: What is the difference between Nominal Value and Real Purchasing Power?
faq.answer: Nominal value is the face dollar amount on your statement, whereas real purchasing power adjusts for CPI price increases to show what those dollars actually buy in today's goods.

faq.question: How fast does 4% annual inflation halve the value of cash?
faq.answer: Using the Rule of 72 (72 ÷ 4), purchasing power drops roughly in half in just 18 years if money earns zero interest.

faq.question: How do I beat inflation when saving long term?
faq.answer: Your investments must achieve a nominal return above the annual inflation rate (plus taxes) so that your real inflation-adjusted return stays positive.

credit-card-payoff.guideTitle: How Credit Card APR Compounds & How to Escape Minimum Payments
credit-card-payoff.guideDesc: Credit card interest accrues on your daily or monthly revolving balance. Paying slightly more than the minimum dramatically shrinks both payoff months and total interest paid.
formulaLines: Monthly Rate (r) = APR ÷ 12
Months to Payoff (n) = -ln(1 - (r × B) ÷ M) ÷ ln(1 + r)
Required Monthly Payment (M) = (r × B) ÷ (1 - (1 + r)^(-n))
Total Interest Paid = (M × n) - Starting Balance (B)

faq.question: Why does paying only the minimum keep credit card debt alive for years?
faq.answer: Because minimum payments are often just 2%–3% of the balance, so most of the early payment goes purely to APR interest rather than reducing principal.

faq.question: What happens if my monthly payment is less than one month of interest?
faq.answer: Negative amortization occurs: your balance actually grows every month instead of shrinking, making payoff impossible without raising the monthly payment.

faq.question: When should I use Credit Card Payoff vs Debt Snowball?
faq.answer: Use this calculator to model one card with a fixed payment or deadline; use Debt Snowball when coordinating payoff order across multiple loans and cards simultaneously.

bmr.guideTitle: BMR vs TDEE Explained: Calculating Your Daily Calorie Target
bmr.guideDesc: Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) is the energy your body burns at complete rest, while Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) multiplies BMR by your weekly movement and workout intensity.
formulaLines: Men BMR = (10 × Weight kg) + (6.25 × Height cm) - (5 × Age) + 5
Women BMR = (10 × Weight kg) + (6.25 × Height cm) - (5 × Age) - 161
TDEE = BMR × Activity Factor (1.2 Sedentary to 1.9 Very Active)
Weight Loss Target ≈ TDEE - 500 kcal/day (~0.45 kg/week)

faq.question: Should I eat at my BMR or my TDEE to lose weight safely?
faq.answer: Never consistently eat below your BMR without medical supervision. Instead, subtract 300–500 kcal from your TDEE (maintenance calories) for sustainable fat loss.

faq.question: Why does Mifflin-St Jeor replace the older Harris-Benedict formula?
faq.answer: Clinical nutrition studies show Mifflin-St Jeor estimates resting energy expenditure within 10% more accurately for modern body compositions.

faq.question: How should I pick between BMI Calculator and BMR / TDEE Calculator?
faq.answer: Use BMI for a quick weight-for-height health category screening; use BMR/TDEE to plan daily food calories and macro budgets.

water-intake.guideTitle: How Daily Hydration Needs Scale With Body Weight, Exercise & Heat
water-intake.guideDesc: Daily fluid needs depend heavily on body mass, sweat loss during physical training, and ambient temperature or humidity rather than a single flat '8 glasses' rule.
formulaLines: Baseline Water (Liters) = Weight (kg) × 0.033
Exercise Adjustment = +0.35 Liters per 30 minutes of moderate/intense workout
Hot / Humid Climate Buffer = +0.50 Liters/day
250ml Glasses = Total Daily Liters × 4

faq.question: Why is weight × 0.033 more accurate than drinking 8 glasses for everyone?
faq.answer: A 55 kg person and a 95 kg athlete have very different blood volume and metabolic heat; weight-based dosing adjusts baseline hydration proportionally.

faq.question: Does coffee or food water count toward daily hydration?
faq.answer: Roughly 20% of daily fluid intake comes from water-rich foods like fruit and vegetables, while pure water and herbal teas fulfill the remaining 80% directly.

faq.question: Can drinking too much water at once be harmful?
faq.answer: Yes, spacing hydration steadily through the day avoids diluting blood sodium (hyponatremia) compared to chugging several liters rapidly.

date-difference.guideTitle: Calculating Exact Calendar Days vs Working Business Days
date-difference.guideDesc: Calendar duration counts every day between two dates including leap days, whereas business-day counting filters out weekends (Saturdays and Sundays) for SLA, payroll, and legal deadlines.
formulaLines: Total Calendar Days = (End UTC Date - Start UTC Date) ÷ 86,400,000 ms
Total Weeks = Total Days ÷ 7, Approximate Years = Total Days ÷ 365.25
Business Days = Sum of all dates t in range where weekday(t) ∈ {Mon..Fri}

faq.question: How are leap years handled in exact day counts?
faq.answer: Using UTC midnight calendar timestamps ensures February 29 in leap years (such as 2024 and 2028) is counted accurately as 366 days without daylight-saving hour drift.

faq.question: What is the difference between calendar days and business days?
faq.answer: Calendar days include Saturdays and Sundays; business days count only Monday–Friday workdays used in shipping estimates, contracts, and legal notices.

faq.question: Are the start and end dates counted inclusively or exclusively?
faq.answer: Standard duration measures elapsed days between Start Date and End Date (e.g., Jan 1 to Jan 2 = 1 day elapsed).

bill-splitter.guideTitle: Splitting Group Restaurant Bills & Gratuity Fairly
bill-splitter.guideDesc: Adding gratuity accurately before dividing by party size prevents awkward shortfalls at the table and lets diners verify both pre-tip and total per-person shares.
formulaLines: Total Tip = Bill Amount × (Tip % ÷ 100)
Grand Total = Bill Amount + Total Tip
Amount per Person = Grand Total ÷ Number of People
Tip per Person = Total Tip ÷ Number of People

faq.question: Should restaurant tip be calculated before or after sales tax?
faq.answer: Etiquette standard calculates gratuity on the pre-tax subtotal, though many diners conveniently tip on the final tax-included check.

faq.question: What is a standard tip percentage for dine-in service?
faq.answer: In the US, 15%–20% is standard; in Israel, 10%–15% (commonly 12%) is customary; in much of Europe, 5%–10% or rounding up applies when service is not included.

faq.question: How does Bill Splitter differ from the basic Tip Calculator?
faq.answer: Both compute tip and split; Bill Splitter emphasizes quick multi-diner group sharing with preset gratuity buttons, while Tip Calculator uses an interactive slider.

currency-converter.guideTitle: How Mid-Market FX Exchange Rates & Cross-Rates Work
currency-converter.guideDesc: Currency conversion multiplies your base amount by the live interbank mid-market exchange rate. Checking the inverse rate helps spot bank markups when traveling or paying international invoices.
formulaLines: Converted Amount = Source Amount × Exchange Rate (Base → Target)
Inverse Rate (Target → Base) = 1 ÷ Exchange Rate (Base → Target)
Bank Markup (%) = [ (Quoted Rate - Mid-Market Rate) ÷ Mid-Market Rate ] × 100

faq.question: What is the mid-market exchange rate vs bank tourist rate?
faq.answer: The mid-market rate is the midpoint between global buy and sell FX quotes. Traditional banks and airport kiosks typically add a 2%–6% spread markup on top.

faq.question: Why should I pay in local currency instead of home currency abroad?
faq.answer: Choosing local currency on card terminals avoids Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC), which often applies an unfavorable 4%–8% exchange markup.

faq.question: How do I compare salaries across countries accurately?
faq.answer: FX conversion shows raw nominal exchange value, whereas our Global Purchasing Power Calculator adjusts for local rent and grocery costs.

sleep-calculator.guideTitle: How 90-Minute Sleep Cycles Determine Optimal Bed & Wake Times
sleep-calculator.guideDesc: Human sleep progresses through 90-minute cycles of light, deep, and REM sleep. Waking at the boundary between cycles—rather than mid-deep-sleep—reduces morning sleep inertia.
formulaLines: Cycle Length = 90 minutes | Average Sleep Onset Latency = 14–15 minutes
Wake-Up Time = Bedtime + 15 min + (N × 90 min), where N ∈ {4, 5, 6}
Bedtime Target = Alarm Time - 15 min - (N × 90 min)
5 Cycles = 7 hours 30 minutes of actual sleep | 6 Cycles = 9 hours

faq.question: Why do I feel groggy after sleeping 8 hours but refreshed after 7.5 hours?
faq.answer: Eight hours frequently cuts straight through the middle of your 6th deep/REM cycle, triggering sleep inertia, whereas 7.5 hours completes 5 full 90-minute cycles cleanly.

faq.question: Why does the calculator add 15 minutes to bedtime?
faq.answer: Most healthy adults require roughly 14–15 minutes to transition from lying down to stage-1 sleep, so counting cycles from lights-out prevents cutting the final cycle short.

faq.question: How many sleep cycles do adults ideally need per night?
faq.answer: Most adults thrive on 5 to 6 complete cycles (7.5 to 9 hours of sleep), while 4 cycles (6 hours) serves as a short-term minimum.

cooking-timer.guideTitle: Roasting Time & Core Temperature Guide for Beef, Poultry, Lamb & Pork
cooking-timer.guideDesc: Safe and juicy oven roasting scales linearly by meat weight and cut thickness, paired with exact internal thermometer readings and carry-over resting time.
formulaLines: Total Roasting Minutes = Base Prep Time + (Weight in kg × Minutes per kg by Cut & Doneness)
Beef Targets: Rare 52°C (125°F) | Medium-Rare 57°C (135°F) | Medium 63°C (145°F)
Poultry Safe Core Temp: 74°C (165°F) | Pork Safe Core: 63°C (145°F)
Resting Time = 10–20 minutes tented loosely in foil (+3°C carry-over cooking)

faq.question: Why should roast meat rest 10–15 minutes after leaving the oven?
faq.answer: Resting lets muscle fibers relax and reabsorb juices while residual heat raises the center temperature another 2°C–4°C (carry-over cooking).

faq.question: Is weight or an instant-read thermometer more reliable?
faq.answer: Weight-based timing estimates when to check the oven, while probing the thickest non-bone center with a meat thermometer confirms food safety and exact doneness.

faq.question: Do stuffed or bone-in cuts take longer per kilogram?
faq.answer: Yes, stuffed poultry or thick bone-in roasts generally need an extra 15–20 minutes total compared with boneless cuts.

severance-pay.guideTitle: How Statutory Severance Pay & Section 14 Pension Deposits Work
severance-pay.guideDesc: Severance entitlement is typically calculated as one month's qualifying salary multiplied by years of tenure. Under Section 14 arrangements, monthly employer pension deposits (8.33%) cover ongoing severance accrual.
formulaLines: Full Gross Severance = Qualifying Monthly Salary × (Years + Months ÷ 12)
Annual Accrual Rate = 100% ÷ 12 = 8.333% of monthly salary
Employer Direct Top-Up = Full Severance - Accumulated Severance Fund Balance

faq.question: What salary components count toward qualifying severance pay?
faq.answer: Base salary, fixed cost-of-living allowances, and regular seniority additions are included, while genuine overtime, car allowances, and expense reimbursements are generally excluded.

faq.question: What is the difference between Section 14 and non-Section-14 severance?
faq.answer: Under Section 14, monthly 8.33% deposits satisfy the severance obligation even on resignation (leaving the fund with the employee), whereas without it, termination triggers a top-up to final salary × years.

faq.question: How are partial years of service calculated?
faq.answer: Every completed month after the initial qualifying year adds 1/12 of a monthly salary proportionally.

stock-options-rsu.guideTitle: Startup Equity Valuation: Vesting, Dilution & Section 102 Capital Gains Tax
stock-options-rsu.guideDesc: True equity take-home value depends on vested shares, strike price spread, future funding dilution, and whether proceeds qualify for a 25% capital gains route or ordinary income tax.
stock-options-rsu.formulaHeading: Vesting, Dilution & Net Equity Exit Formulas
formulaLines: Vested Shares = Total Grant × [ (Months Elapsed >= Cliff ? Months Elapsed : 0) ÷ Total Vesting Months ]
Diluted Share Price = Exit Price × (1 - Dilution % ÷ 100)
Options Gross Spread = max(0, Diluted Exit Price - Strike Price) × Vested Options
RSU Gross Value = Diluted Exit Price × Vested RSUs | Net = Gross × (1 - Tax Rate)

faq.question: What is the 1-year cliff in a standard 4-year vesting schedule?
faq.answer: During the first 12 months, 0% of your grant vests; on month 12, 25% unlocks at once, followed by monthly (1/48) or quarterly installments over the remaining 3 years.

faq.question: How does Israel Section 102 Capital Gains (25%) differ from Section 102 Income?
faq.answer: Under the Capital Gains Trustee route held for at least 24 months, gains above the grant-date average price are taxed at 25% (plus 3% surtax above threshold) instead of up to 47%–50% marginal income tax.

faq.question: Why do RSUs keep value even if the stock drops, unlike options?
faq.answer: Options only pay the spread above the strike price (zero if underwater), whereas each RSU has full underlying share value as long as the share price exceeds $0.

purchase-appreciation-tax.guideTitle: Tiered Real Estate Purchase Tax & Linear Appreciation Tax Explained
purchase-appreciation-tax.guideDesc: Israel property purchase tax (Mas Rechisha) is calculated progressively across statutory brackets that differ sharply between a sole residence and an investment home, while appreciation tax (Mas Shevach) taxes net capital profit after deductible costs.
formulaLines: Purchase Tax = Sum over each bracket i of [ (min(Price, Cap_i) - Floor_i) × Rate_i ]
Net Appreciation Gain = Sale Price - Purchase Price - Legal, Brokerage & Renovation Costs
Linear Tax Ratio (post-2014) = Taxable Days after Jan 1, 2014 ÷ Total Ownership Days
Appreciation Tax = Net Gain × Linear Ratio × 25%

faq.question: Why is single-home purchase tax calculated in tiers rather than one flat rate?
faq.answer: The tax-free threshold applies to the bottom slice of a sole home, and each higher slice pays only the marginal bracket rate (e.g., 3.5%, 5%, 8%, 10%), whereas investment apartments start taxing from the very first shekel at 8%.

faq.question: What expenses reduce Appreciation Tax (Mas Shevach)?
faq.answer: Documented purchase tax paid, buyer and seller attorney fees, broker commissions, appraisal fees, and capital improvement renovations with valid tax invoices.

faq.question: How does linear preferential appreciation tax benefit pre-2014 owners?
faq.answer: Days held before January 1, 2014 are tax-exempt under the linear formula, so only the proportional gain accrued after 2014 is taxed at 25%.

employer-cost.guideTitle: Gross Salary vs Total Employer Cost & Employee Net Take-Home Pay
employer-cost.guideDesc: An employee's gross salary is only part of total payroll cost: employers contribute mandatory pension, severance, study fund, and employer National Insurance on top, while employees pay progressive income tax and social security.
formulaLines: Total Employer Cost = Gross Salary + Employer Pension (6.5%) + Severance (8.33%) + Study Fund (7.5%) + Employer NI
Employer Multiplier = Total Employer Cost ÷ Gross Salary (typically 1.24x–1.30x)
Employee Net Pay = Gross Salary - Income Tax - Employee NI/Health - Employee Pension (6%) - Employee Study Fund (2.5%)

faq.question: Why does hiring an employee cost 25%–30% more than gross salary?
faq.answer: Mandatory statutory social contributions (pension 6.5%, severance 8.33%, employer National Insurance 3.55%–7.6%) plus optional study fund (7.5%) add roughly 24%–30% above base gross.

faq.question: What is the difference between Salary Converter and Employer Cost?
faq.answer: Salary Converter translates pay frequency (hourly/monthly/annual), whereas Employer Cost breaks down full payroll taxes, pension provisions, and true net bank deposit.

faq.question: Does pension contribution reduce taxable income?
faq.answer: Employee pension deposits earn statutory tax credits/deductions within legal caps, improving net take-home pay compared with un sheltered income.

z-score.guideTitle: Z-Scores, Standard Normal Distribution & Bell-Curve Probabilities
z-score.guideDesc: A Z-score measures exactly how many standard deviations a raw score sits above or below the population mean, letting you compare data across completely different scales via the standard normal curve.
formulaLines: Standard Z-Score: Z = (X - μ) ÷ σ
Inverse Raw Score: X = μ + (Z × σ)
Cumulative Left-Tail Probability: Φ(z) = P(Z ≤ z) = ½ [ 1 + erf(z ÷ √2) ]

faq.question: What does a Z-score of +1.5 or -2.0 mean?
faq.answer: A Z-score of +1.5 means the observation is 1.5 standard deviations above the mean (approx. 93.3rd percentile), while -2.0 is 2 standard deviations below the mean (approx. 2.28th percentile).

faq.question: How do I convert a percentile back into a raw score?
faq.answer: Switch to Inverse Mode, enter your target percentile (e.g., 95%), mean μ, and standard deviation σ; the calculator finds Z ≈ 1.645 and computes X = μ + 1.645σ.

faq.question: What is the difference between one-tailed and two-tailed p-values?
faq.answer: One-tailed probability checks extreme values in one direction only (Z > z or Z < z), whereas two-tailed probability doubles the tail area to test deviation in either direction.

linear-regression.guideTitle: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression & R-Squared
linear-regression.guideDesc: Linear regression fits the straight line y = mx + b that minimizes squared vertical errors across your (x, y) data points, while Pearson r and R² quantify linear correlation strength.
linear-regression.formulaHeading: OLS Regression, Pearson r & R² Formulas
formulaLines: Slope (m) = Σ[(x_i - x̄)(y_i - ȳ)] ÷ Σ[(x_i - x̄)²]
Y-Intercept (b) = ȳ - m × x̄  |  Line: ŷ = mx + b
Pearson Correlation (r) = Σ[(x_i - x̄)(y_i - ȳ)] ÷ √[ Σ(x_i - x̄)² × Σ(y_i - ȳ)² ]
Coefficient of Determination = R² = r² (fraction of variance explained)

faq.question: What is the difference between Pearson r and R-squared (R²)?
faq.answer: Pearson r ranges from -1 to +1 and shows both direction (positive or negative) and linear strength; R² ranges from 0 to 1 and tells what percentage of Y variation is explained by X.

faq.question: How many data points are needed for a linear regression line?
faq.answer: Mathematically at least 2 distinct X points define a line, though 5+ points are needed for meaningful correlation and R² diagnostics.

faq.question: Does high R² prove X causes Y?
faq.answer: No—regression measures linear association and predictive fit, not causation or non-linear curved relationships.

quadratic-equation.guideTitle: Solving Quadratic Equations: Discriminant, Complex Roots & Parabola Vertex
quadratic-equation.guideDesc: Every quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 forms a parabola whose discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac reveals whether the curve crosses the x-axis twice, touches once, or produces complex conjugate roots.
formulaLines: Discriminant: Δ = b² - 4ac
Parabola Vertex (h, k): h = -b ÷ (2a),  k = a·h² + b·h + c
Axis of Symmetry: x = h  |  Y-Intercept: (0, c)

faq.question: What do the three cases of the discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac mean?
faq.answer: Δ > 0 gives two distinct real roots; Δ = 0 gives one repeated real root sitting right at the vertex on the x-axis; Δ < 0 gives two complex conjugate roots (no real x-intercepts).

faq.question: How do you know if the parabola opens upward or downward?
faq.answer: If the leading coefficient a > 0, the parabola opens upward and the vertex is a minimum; if a < 0, it opens downward and the vertex is a maximum.

faq.question: What happens if a = 0?
faq.answer: The equation is no longer quadratic—it becomes linear (bx + c = 0) with the single root x = -c ÷ b.

linear-system.guideTitle: Solving 2×2 Linear Equation Systems With Cramer's Rule & Determinants
linear-system.guideDesc: A 2×2 linear system seeks the point (x, y) where two lines intersect. Cramer's Rule computes determinants D, Dx, and Dy directly to give exact solutions or flag parallel lines.
formulaLines: System: a₁x + b₁y = c₁  and  a₂x + b₂y = c₂
Main Determinant: D = a₁b₂ - a₂b₁
Dx = c₁b₂ - c₂b₁  |  Dy = a₁c₂ - a₂c₁
Unique Solution (when D ≠ 0): x = Dx ÷ D,  y = Dy ÷ D

faq.question: What happens when the main determinant D equals 0?
faq.answer: If D = 0 and either Dx ≠ 0 or Dy ≠ 0, the lines are parallel and never cross (no solution). If D = Dx = Dy = 0, both equations describe the same line (infinitely many solutions).

faq.question: Why use Cramer's Rule instead of substitution?
faq.answer: Cramer's Rule works in fixed closed-form determinant arithmetic without fractions until the very final division, preventing early rounding error.

faq.question: Can this solve 3×3 matrix operations too?
faq.answer: For 3×3 determinant, inverse, and matrix multiplication, switch to our Matrix Calculator.

base-converter.guideTitle: Positional Number Systems: Binary, Octal, Decimal & Hexadecimal
base-converter.guideDesc: Every positional numeral system represents values as sums of digit × baseᵖ. Computer systems rely on Base 2 (binary), Base 8 (octal), and Base 16 (hexadecimal) because 1 hex digit cleanly packs 4 bits.
formulaLines: 1 Hex Digit (0–9, A–F) = Exactly 4 Binary Bits (1 Nibble)
2 Hex Digits (00–FF) = 8 Bits (1 Byte, values 0–255)
1 Octal Digit (0–7) = Exactly 3 Binary Bits

faq.question: Why do programmers use Hexadecimal (Base 16) instead of raw Binary?
faq.answer: Every single hex character maps 1-to-1 onto 4 binary bits, compressing a 32-bit memory address or RGB color (#FF5733) into just 6–8 compact characters.

faq.question: Which characters are valid in bases above 10 (up to Base 36)?
faq.answer: Digits 0–9 represent values 0–9, and letters A–Z represent values 10–35 (for instance, A = 10, F = 15, Z = 35).

faq.question: Does this converter handle 64-bit numbers without losing precision?
faq.answer: Yes, it uses JavaScript BigInt rather than 53-bit floats, keeping large 64-bit and 128-bit integer conversions exact.

bitwise-calculator.guideTitle: Bitwise Logic Gates, Bitmasks & Shift Operators (8 / 16 / 32-Bit)
bitwise-calculator.guideDesc: Bitwise operations manipulate individual 0/1 bits inside fixed-width integers simultaneously, powering hardware registers, network subnet masks, permissions, and fast bit-flags.
formulaLines: AND (&): 1 only when BOTH bits are 1 (used to read/clear masked bits)
OR (|): 1 when AT LEAST ONE bit is 1 (used to set flag bits ON)
XOR (^): 1 when bits DIFFER (used to toggle bits or check inequality)
NOT (~): Flips every bit within active bit-width | Left Shift (<< k) ≈ × 2ᵏ

faq.question: When do engineers use AND, OR, and XOR bitmasks?
faq.answer: Use OR (flags | MASK) to enable a feature bit, AND (flags & ~MASK) to clear a bit, AND (flags & MASK) to test if a bit is set, and XOR (flags ^ MASK) to toggle it.

faq.question: Why does bit-width (8-bit vs 16-bit vs 32-bit) change NOT (~) results?
faq.answer: Bitwise NOT flips every bit in the register, so 8-bit ~0b00000101 becomes 0b11111010 (250 unsigned), whereas 16-bit flips 16 bits.

faq.question: What is the arithmetic equivalent of << and >> bit shifts?
faq.answer: Shifting left by k bits multiplies by 2ᵏ (modulo bit-width), while unsigned shifting right divides by 2ᵏ and drops the remainder.

triangle-solver.guideTitle: Solving Any Triangle: Law of Cosines, Law of Sines & Heron's Formula
triangle-solver.guideDesc: Given three sides (SSS) or two sides with their included angle (SAS), classical trigonometry reconstructs every missing side, interior angle, altitude, inradius, and circumradius.
formulaLines: Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² - 2ab·cos(C)  |  cos(A) = (b² + c² - a²) ÷ 2bc
Semi-perimeter: s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2
Heron's Area Formula: Area = √[ s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c) ]
Inradius: r = Area ÷ s  |  Circumradius: R = (abc) ÷ (4 × Area)

faq.question: What is the Triangle Inequality rule that makes a triangle valid?
faq.answer: The sum of any two side lengths must strictly exceed the third side (a + b > c, a + c > b, b + c > a); otherwise the segments cannot close into a triangle.

faq.question: What is the difference between Inradius (r) and Circumradius (R)?
faq.answer: The inradius r is the radius of the largest circle fitting inside tangent to all three sides, while the circumradius R passes through all three triangle vertices.

faq.question: How are triangle heights (altitudes) calculated?
faq.answer: Each altitude equals twice the area divided by its corresponding base side: h_a = 2·Area ÷ a.

circle-sector.guideTitle: Circle Sector Geometry: Arc Length, Sector Area, Chord & Segment
circle-sector.guideDesc: A circle sector is a pizza-slice wedge bounded by two radii and an arc, whereas a circular segment is the region trapped between the curved arc and the straight chord line.
circle-sector.formulaHeading: Sector, Arc, Chord & Segment Formulas (θ in Radians)
formulaLines: Radians Conversion: θ_rad = θ_deg × (π ÷ 180)
Arc Length: s = r × θ_rad
Sector Area: A_sector = ½ × r² × θ_rad
Chord Length: c = 2r × sin(θ_rad ÷ 2)  |  Segment Area = ½ × r² × (θ_rad - sin θ_rad)

faq.question: What is the difference between a Circular Sector and a Circular Segment?
faq.answer: A sector reaches all the way to the circle's center like a pie slice; a segment removes the inner triangle, leaving only the curved cap between the arc and the chord.

faq.question: Why must angles be converted to radians in s = rθ?
faq.answer: Because radian measure is defined as arc-to-radius ratio (full circle = 2π rad), turning arc length and sector area into clean formulas without extra 360° factors.

faq.question: When does the chord equal the circle's diameter?
faq.answer: At a central angle of 180° (π radians), where sin(90°) = 1 so chord length c = 2r.

matrix-calculator.guideTitle: Matrix Algebra: Multiplication, Determinants, Inverses & Rank
matrix-calculator.guideDesc: Linear transformations, systems of equations, and 3D computer graphics rely on exact matrix operations such as dot-product multiplication, determinants, and Gauss-Jordan inversion.
formulaLines: Product (A × B)[i,j] = Σ (A[i,k] × B[k,j]) for matching inner dimensions
2×2 Determinant: det(A) = (a × d) - (b × c)
2×2 Inverse: A⁻¹ = (1 ÷ det(A)) × [[d, -b], [-c, a]] when det(A) ≠ 0
3×3 Determinant: Cofactor expansion along first row: a(ei−fh) − b(di−fg) + c(dh−eg)

faq.question: When does a square matrix have no inverse (singular matrix)?
faq.answer: A square matrix has no inverse when its determinant equals zero (det(A) = 0), which happens whenever rows or columns are linearly dependent.

faq.question: Why must columns of Matrix A equal rows of Matrix B for multiplication?
faq.answer: Matrix multiplication computes dot products of each row in A with each column in B, so an m×n matrix can only multiply an n×p matrix, yielding an m×p result.

faq.question: What does the determinant tell you geometrically?
faq.answer: The absolute value of the determinant measures the area (2D) or volume (3D) scaling factor of the linear transformation, and its sign shows whether orientation flips.

complex-numbers.guideTitle: Complex Number Arithmetic: Rectangular, Polar & Euler Forms
complex-numbers.guideDesc: Complex numbers combine a real axis and an imaginary axis (i² = −1) to model AC electrical impedance, signal phases, resonance frequencies, and 2D rotations.
formulaLines: Cartesian Form: z = a + bi (where i² = -1)
Modulus (Magnitude): |z| = √(a² + b²) | Argument Angle: θ = atan2(b, a)
Polar & Euler Forms: z = r(cos θ + i sin θ) = r · e^(iθ)
Division Rule: (a + bi) ÷ (c + di) = [(ac + bd) + (bc - ad)i] ÷ (c² + d²)

faq.question: How do you divide two complex numbers manually?
faq.answer: Multiply both numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate of the denominator (c − di) so the denominator becomes the real number c² + d².

faq.question: When is polar form better than rectangular form?
faq.answer: Rectangular form (a + bi) simplifies addition and subtraction, while polar form (r∠θ) makes multiplication, division, and powers much faster.

faq.question: Why do electrical engineers use j instead of i for complex impedance?
faq.answer: In AC circuit theory, the letter i already denotes electrical current, so engineers write Z = R + jX where j² = −1.

pregnancy.guideTitle: How Pregnancy Weeks, Trimesters & Estimated Due Date Are Calculated
pregnancy.guideDesc: Clinical due dates use Naegele's Rule—counting 280 days (40 weeks) from the first day of your last menstrual period (LMP), with adjustments for irregular cycle lengths or conception dates.
formulaLines: Estimated Due Date (LMP) = LMP Date + 280 days + (Cycle Length − 28 days)
Estimated Due Date (Conception / IVF) = Conception Date + 266 days (or − Embryo Age)
Gestational Week = floor(Days Since Adjusted LMP ÷ 7) + Remaining Days

faq.question: Why does gestational age start two weeks before conception?
faq.answer: Obstetric dating starts from the Last Menstrual Period (LMP) because ovulation timing varies, making a standard 38-week embryonic timeline equal 40 gestational weeks.

faq.question: How does cycle length change the estimated due date?
faq.answer: Because ovulation typically occurs 14 days before the next period, a 32-day cycle shifts ovulation and the due date 4 days later than a standard 28-day cycle.

faq.question: What are the three trimesters by gestational week?
faq.answer: First trimester spans Weeks 1–13, Second trimester Weeks 14–27, and Third trimester Weeks 28–40+ until delivery.

retirement-planner.guideTitle: Retirement Planning, FIRE Corpus & The 4% Safe Withdrawal Rule
retirement-planner.guideDesc: Sustainable retirement planning balances pre-retirement compounding with inflation-adjusted portfolio drawdowns designed to outlast a 30+ year horizon.
formulaLines: Target FIRE Nest Egg = Desired Annual Retirement Spending ÷ Safe Withdrawal Rate (e.g. 0.04 = 25× Expenses)
Accumulated Corpus = Current Savings(1+r)^n + Monthly Deposit × [((1+r)^n − 1) ÷ r]
Real Return Rate = [(1 + Nominal Return) ÷ (1 + Inflation)] − 1

faq.question: What is the 4% Safe Withdrawal Rule (Trinity Study)?
faq.answer: It estimates you can withdraw 4% of your initial portfolio in year one of retirement, then adjust that dollar amount for inflation each year with high historical odds of lasting 30 years.

faq.question: Should I plan retirement contributions using nominal or real returns?
faq.answer: Using real inflation-adjusted returns (e.g., 5% instead of 7%–8%) keeps your target nest egg aligned with today's purchasing power.

faq.question: How do pensions or Social Security change my savings target?
faq.answer: Guaranteed lifetime income directly reduces the annual spending gap your personal investment portfolio needs to fund.

capital-gains-tax.guideTitle: Capital Gains Tax: Real vs Inflationary Gains & Loss Harvesting
capital-gains-tax.guideDesc: Net investment returns depend on cost basis adjustments, tax-loss carryforwards, and whether tax law applies flat rates to real inflation-adjusted gains or nominal profits.
capital-gains-tax.formulaHeading: Taxable Capital Gain & Net Proceeds Formulas
formulaLines: Nominal Gain = Sale Proceeds − Purchase Cost Basis − Broker Commissions
Real (Inflation-Adjusted) Gain = Sale Proceeds − (Adjusted Cost Basis × CPI Index Ratio)
Tax Payable = max(0, Taxable Gain − Offset Losses) × Capital Gains Tax Rate

faq.question: What is the difference between real and nominal capital gains tax?
faq.answer: Nominal tax applies to the raw currency profit, while real capital gains systems (such as 25% real tax in Israel) exempt the portion of price appreciation caused strictly by inflation.

faq.question: How does tax-loss harvesting reduce my tax bill?
faq.answer: Realized capital losses on losing positions can offset realized capital gains in the same tax year or carry forward to future years.

faq.question: Can brokerage commissions be deducted from taxable capital gains?
faq.answer: Yes, verified buy and sell transaction commissions directly increase cost basis or reduce sale proceeds, lowering taxable profit.

car-finance-lease.guideTitle: Car Loan vs Auto Lease: Depreciation, Residual Value & True Net Cost
car-finance-lease.guideDesc: Deciding between financing, operational leasing, and balloon loans requires comparing net cash outflows minus the projected resale equity at the end of ownership.
car-finance-lease.formulaHeading: Lease vs Finance Net Cost Formulas
formulaLines: Loan Monthly Payment = P × [r(1+r)^n ÷ ((1+r)^n − 1)]
Total Lease Outlay = Down Payment + (Monthly Lease Fee × Months) + End Fees
Net True Ownership Cost = Total Cash Paid − Projected Vehicle Resale Value

faq.question: When is buying with a car loan cheaper than leasing?
faq.answer: Buying typically wins over 4–7+ years because once the loan finishes you own a debt-free asset with resale value, whereas leasing requires continuous monthly payments.

faq.question: What is residual value in a car lease?
faq.answer: Residual value is the vehicle's projected wholesale value at the end of the lease; you pay for depreciation down to that value plus the financing factor.

faq.question: What hidden costs should I include when comparing lease vs buy?
faq.answer: Account for mileage overage penalties, wear-and-tear charges, and maintenance packages included in operational leases versus out-of-warranty repairs when owning.

scientific-unit-engine.guideTitle: Engineering & Scientific Unit Conversions Across SI and Imperial Systems
scientific-unit-engine.guideDesc: Precision engineering requires exact dimensional conversion across pressure, energy, power, torque, flow rate, and thermal scales without rounding drift.
formulaLines: Pressure: 1 bar = 100,000 Pa = 14.50377 psi = 0.98692 atm
Energy & Power: 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ = 3,412.14 BTU | 1 HP = 745.7 Watts
Torque & Force: 1 N·m = 0.73756 lb-ft | 1 lbf = 4.44822 Newtons
Temperature Scales: K = °C + 273.15 | °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32

faq.question: What is the difference between kW and kWh?
faq.answer: Kilowatts (kW) measure instantaneous power draw rate, while kilowatt-hours (kWh) measure cumulative energy consumed or stored over time (1 kW × 1 hour = 3.6 MJ).

faq.question: How do gauge pressure (psig) and absolute pressure (psia) differ?
faq.answer: Absolute pressure includes atmospheric pressure (~14.7 psi at sea level), whereas gauge pressure measures only pressure above ambient air.

faq.question: Why are exact SI conversion factors critical in CAD and lab work?
faq.answer: Even small rounding errors between inches, millimeters, Pascals, and PSI compound across tolerances and thermal stress calculations.

purchasing-power.guideTitle: Cost of Living Comparison, Purchasing Power Parity & Relocation Salary
purchasing-power.guideDesc: Comparing job offers across global cities requires adjusting gross pay for local rent, groceries, utilities, tax burdens, and Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) indices.
formulaLines: Equivalent Salary = Current Net Income × (Target City Cost Index ÷ Origin City Cost Index)
Housing-Adjusted Gap = Target Rent Share − Origin Rent Share
Real Disposable Surplus = Target Net Salary − Total Localized Monthly Living Basket

faq.question: Why is a higher nominal salary in New York or Tel Aviv sometimes worth less?
faq.answer: High housing rents, childcare, and consumer price indices absorb a larger share of income, reducing real disposable savings compared to lower-cost cities.

faq.question: What is included in a city Cost of Living index?
faq.answer: Indices combine weighted baskets for housing rent, groceries, restaurant dining, public transit, utilities, and healthcare.

faq.question: How should remote workers evaluate Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)?
faq.answer: Remote professionals earning in a strong currency and living in a lower-cost hub capture higher real savings by comparing local rent plus core living costs against net pay.

tips.title: The Rule of 72 for Investments
tips.content: Want to know when your money doubles? Divide 72 by the annual interest rate.

tips.title: The 50/30/20 Budget Rule
tips.content: Split net income: 50% for needs, 30% for wants, and 20% for savings & investments.

tips.title: The 30% Mortgage Rule
tips.content: Monthly mortgage payments should not exceed 30%-35% of household net monthly income.

tips.title: The 20/4/10 Auto Rule
tips.content: 20% down payment, finance for max 4 years, total monthly auto costs under 10% income.

tips.title: Internet Speed: Mbps to MB/s
tips.content: ISPs sell speeds in Megabits (Mb). Divide by 8 to get real download speed in Megabytes (MB/s).

tips.title: Fast Mental Tip & % Calculation
tips.content: Move decimal 1 spot left for 10%, then double for 20% or add half for 15%.
